our_interpretation: This asserts a necessary revenue threshold for paying compute obligations. It does not predict that OpenAI will reach $75 billion.
The revenue checkpoint is December 31, 2026. Subsequent payment performance may be needed to evaluate the asserted necessity.
Read 'any chance' as financial feasibility, allowing for cash, financing and the timing of obligations.
The purpose clause does not identify a separate external antecedent that must first occur.
No precise tolerance around $75 billion or accounting basis is supplied. A contradiction would require revenue clearly below the approximate threshold, not a borderline difference.
criteria.support_condition: A substantiated funding and payment analysis establishes that OpenAI could not feasibly meet the identified compute obligations with an exit-2026 annualized revenue level materially below roughly $75 billion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: OpenAI exits 2026 materially below roughly $75 billion annualized revenue and nevertheless meets the relevant compute obligations, or binding funding arrangements establish its ability to do so without that revenue threshold.
